findings.evidence: The Routines list reports '1 total · 0 active · 1 draft', offers all/draft/completed/archived filters, and labels the row 'Draft'; the Active category is counted but not offered as a filter. The same routine's overview shows all three Week 1 days as 'Logged: Done' and a primary 'Next: Lower body · Week 2'. Only the overview qualifies the state as 'Plan: Draft'. The false 'Not started' wording is gone, but this round-2 objection is only partly resolved.
findings.userConsequence: A person who has logged three sessions sees the plan counted as inactive and cannot isolate an active plan, so the list reads as unstarted while the overview says training is underway.
findings.suggestedChange: Use one vocabulary across the summary, filters, row, and detail: show 'Plan: draft' on the list row and either add an Active filter or stop counting active separately, keeping training progress (next week) distinct from plan status.

findings.evidence: At 390×844 the Warm-up and Main lift cards fill the viewport. The Accessory title and its '2×10 35 lb rest 90s' prescription are the last visible content; its set chips and rest control sit behind the fixed footer. Merging prescription and prescribed note reduced height, but three exercises still do not fit as in the baseline.
findings.userConsequence: Logging the third lift requires a scroll before any of its set fields are reachable, and a mid-session glance shows only two exercises.
findings.suggestedChange: Condense the day header further and trim repeated card spacing while keeping the 15px set values, then add bottom padding so the last card clears the footer.

findings.evidence: The catalogue opens with a 'needs review 4' row above every muscle group. The page copy says only 'Browse movements, versions and exercise details', so the label is not explained and reads as an internal maintenance bucket.
findings.userConsequence: A browsing user may interpret it as an outstanding task and open a catalog-maintenance list instead of an exercise group.
findings.suggestedChange: Rename it to something self-explanatory such as 'Exercises to confirm (4)' with one line of help, or move it below the muscle groups.

findings.evidence: On the Accessory card the prescription says 'rest 90s' while its rest control shows '1:30'. The Main lift consistently pairs 'rest 2:00' with '2:00'. Both formats are visible in the same screen in light and dark.
findings.userConsequence: The timer appears to disagree with the prescription, so a user may think the rest was adjusted or misread the target.
findings.suggestedChange: Use one convention in the prescription line and the control, for example 'rest 1:30' and '1:30', or show seconds in both.

strengths: Onboarding pairs each of the three steps with a labeled action and keeps the current step visually primary; the manual builder is offered without competing with the guided path.
Prompts makes copy the first action, with a character count and a direct Go to Import step, preserving the offline AI workflow without implying an in-app AI call.

Import handles error, resolution, and confirmation distinctly: a bordered recovery alert with the recovery prompt as primary, a gated Resolve step, and a confirmation that names Squat's catalog link and states that further review is optional.
The desktop shell is stable: fixed sidebar, one content origin, an 840px content measure, no duplicate hamburger, and exercise tools beside their names.
Light and dark themes keep the same hierarchy; the dark Workout, Routine, Library, and Workspace screens are legible and the terminal theme chip is visibly selected.
Workout logging labels History, More, Set rest, Start, and Reset, keeps 15px set values, and the warm-up rest control is now a bordered clock button rather than dotted text.
Routine overview names the next day and week, states logged days in text, and keeps analysis to a single summary row with a View analysis action.
History sort labels are explicit, exercise-history volume includes lb, library equipment filters are text chips that fit on two rows, and the bodyweight card states start, current, change, and range.
Workspace distinguishes backup, destructive import, snapshots, and local-first limits, with the current theme visible as selected.
limitations: Inspected all 27 frozen manifest images with the image viewer; every file was readable.

Read the nine prior raw reviews, all three prior assessments, and the round 3 implementation response. Prior-round screenshots were not reopened for pixel comparison, so no direct image-to-image regression claim is made.
No other current-round reviewer output and no parent conversation were read.
No regression was established from the supplied current images. The prior objections that remain are recorded in R03-DS-01 and R03-DS-02.
Contrast is a visual judgment only; no ratios, accessibility conformance, keyboard behavior, persistence, or tap-target sizes were measured or exercised.
Evidence covers 390×844 mobile light and dark and 1280×900 desktop light only; dark coverage is four screens and desktop coverage is four routes.
The Workspace theme chips are cut by the bottom edge of the 844px capture; the selected chip is visible, but the rest of the Appearance controls cannot be verified.
